title: Implement safe plugin isolation and migration harness for GPU runtime
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Upgrades to CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA have exposed intermittent symbol conflicts and cold-start flakiness when multiple model variants are deployed on heterogenous GPU nodes. Existing kernel-load paths attempt aggressive shared-object binding which can leave processes in partially-initialized states and complicate rollback.

Goal: Create an isolation-and-migration harness that allows us to stage new kernel bundles (CUTLASS/Triton plugins) alongside in-use bundles, run deterministic canary validations, and provide safe, automated rollback. The harness should: (1) provide per-process plugin sandboxes with namespacing for exported symbols, (2) implement a staged prelink step to detect link-time conflicts before handshake, (3) support binary migration hooks so a node can atomically swap active bundle pointer with fallback, and (4) surface clear telemetry and guardrails for ops to decide safe rollouts.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full on-disk bundle signing or HSM verification (follow-up). It also does not change model-serving logic beyond safe load/unload semantics.
acceptance_criteria: New plugin loader can register two versions of the same CUTLASS/Triton bundle and keep them isolated in a single process
Deterministic prelink step can detect symbol collisions and fail a canary without touching live traffic
Automated rollback path toggles bundle pointer and validates KV-cache reuse or safe evict without leaking handles
Benchmarks show no more than 5% median tail-latency regression at P50/P95 on representative L0 workloads during canary switching
Runbook added to Console Operations playbooks and a smoke-runner job created in CI to exercise staged migrations
risks: Namespace isolation could add indirection cost; must verify symbol resolver overhead
KV cache format changes may require small on-disk migration steps for long-running models
Edge cases where third-party Triton plugins open raw CUDA contexts may escape sandboxing
Rollback during heavy inference load could temporarily increase OOM/eviction rates
rollout_plan: Spike/implementation on dev cluster with synthetic L0 models (dev-01)
Canary on staging: enable harness for 10% of nodes, run 24h smoke + perf benchmarks
Controlled rollout on Dedicated pool with progressive node groups (25% -> 50% -> 100%)
Full production flip after 72h canary with no regression signals and manual ops approval
comments: 2026-03-10 Liam Chen: Created ticket after last week's production incident where partial kernel link left worker in SKIPPED_INIT state. Spike shows two probable causes: aggressive dlopen() ordering and global symbol collisions.

2026-03-11 Priya Nandagopal: Completed design spike. Prototype demonstrates per-plugin symbol prefixing using GNU symbol versioning and a thin indirection layer for exports. Performance microbenchmark shows ~2% CPU overhead on symbol-heavy entry points.

2026-03-12 Marco Rivera (Infra Review): Concern about added indirection impacting kernel hot paths for small-token workloads. Requested a microbenchmark across p10/p50/p95 token-length distributions and comparison with lazy-binding approach.

2026-03-12 Priya: Implemented staged prelink test harness and added a failing-mode that exercises collision detection. Opened design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Plugin+Isolation+Design
2026-03-13 Priya: Opened PR #18934 that wires the new loader behind a feature-flag (runtime.isolated_plugin_loader). Added unit tests and simple canary smoke job in CI: ci/gpu-plugin-migration.yml

2026-03-14 SRE: Canary smoke run shows a 6% P95 regression for <8-token responses on g5x-large. Investigating kernel-boundary inlining that gets disabled by symbol indirection. Temporary mitigation: enable kernel-level fastpath when sequence length < 16 via runtime flag.

2026-03-14 Liam: Action items: 1) Add microbenchmark targeted at small-token fastpath and test alternative lazy-binding (dlopen+RTLD_NOW vs RTLD_LAZY) and versioned-symbol approach; 2) Draft ops runbook for progressive rollback; 3) Schedule perf review with runtime team (2026-03-16)
